Diagnosis hints

Read a spectrum first.

Coast-down / run-up (Bode plot)

Start recording while the machine runs at full speed, then switch the motor off. The app reads speed + 1x amplitude / phase continuously and stops by itself when the speed is gone (or press Stop). Same 1x conversion as the Meter.

Each line is one spectrum (newest in front). For a coast‑down, start recording and switch the machine off — speed is stored with every line.

Saved measurement points

Points are kept in this browser only. Export regularly. Use them in the Report tab (“copy a saved point”).

Balancing job

Measure every weight angle from the reference mark (tacho tape / position 1) in one fixed direction — always the same direction for trial and correction weights. If a check run makes the vibration worse, set Angle direction to Mirrored and recalculate.

Step

Fill in the job data and press New job.

Live 3D

Arrows = measured 1x vibration at each sensor (length ∝ mm/s, angle = phase from the tacho mark); grey = initial run. This is the measured vibration, not the heavy-spot position. Tap a run to show it. The 3D only reads the job – nothing is changed.

Correction

–

Weight vector calculator – add / combine weights

Combine weights that are (or will be) on the same plane into one equivalent weight, e.g. correction + trim, or an old weight already welded + a new one. Use “Remove” for a weight you take off.

Polar plot (1x vibration)

Red = Left sensor, blue = Right sensor. 0 = initial run, T1/T2 = trial runs, K1… = check runs. Green / purple ticks on the rim = correction angle plane 1 / plane 2.

Correction disc (blades / holes around 360°):
drag the 3D disc to rotate

Model dimensions (drive the 3D geometry)

Correction radius, holes, angles and masses always come from the Balance tab. Without Ø the model is schematic: angles and holes are correct, sizes are not to scale. Missing values are never invented – the panel shows SCHEMATIC / NOT AVAILABLE.

3D controls

1500 rpm (demo)

One finger drag = turn 360° · two fingers = zoom / move · tap a part to highlight and focus it. The 3D view and the cinematic sequence only read the balancing job – nothing here changes measurements, calculations or the job. Real speed is shown slowed down on screen; the rpm number is the real value (LIVE = instrument, LAST RUN = last balancing run, DEMO = not a reading).

Sensors

Sensor calibration

Put the sensor on a reference shaker (or measure next to a calibrated instrument) with a known vibration, enter that value and press Measure. The app proposes a corrected sensitivity – nothing changes until you press Apply. Only the sensitivity setting changes; no formula is changed.

Balancing reject limits

A balancing run that breaks any of these limits is rejected and no correction is calculated from it. Tighter = more reliable, looser = accepts noisier machines.

Factory reset

“Reset settings” keeps all points, balancing jobs, coefficients and reports. “Erase all data” deletes everything this app stored on this device (asks twice).

Units and basis

The instrument reports RMS (Peak = RMS × √2, P‑P = RMS × 2√2).

ISO severity class

Machine data for fault markers

Bearing (enter geometry or multipliers)

Multipliers (× running speed) from the bearing maker's calculator override geometry.

Type a bearing number: if it is in your library the geometry / multipliers fill in automatically. New bearing: enter the values from the maker's catalogue once, then Save. The app never guesses bearing geometry.

Measurement quality

Spike rejection drops readings such as the 1995 / 6436 value seen at switch‑off. Energy factor scales spectrum‑based overall values (1.00 = no correction).

Display & voice

Data backup / restore

One file with everything: saved points, balancing jobs, saved rotor coefficients, settings and all reports (with photos). Use it to move data between phone and laptop, or as a safety copy.
